Leak sensors have always been one of the most worthwhile smart home products, and Shelly's new Flood S Gen4 lowers the entry barrier even further. It costs less than US$30, is Matter-certified, and supports Apple Home right out of the box.

HomeKit Weekly is a series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Larger sensing area

Most leak sensors on the market use small metal probes on the bottom, which means water must accumulate at just the right spot to trigger them. Shelly has taken a different approach this time, placing three large stainless steel sensing pads on the bottom of the sensor. The greater the contact area, the faster it detects leaks and the wider the coverage — which is precisely why you'd place a sensor under your water heater or washing machine.

These sensing pads are even sensitive enough to detect pure water or low-conductivity water, such as condensation from an air conditioner. These types of leaks are typically harder to spot. The Flood S Gen4 is slim enough to slide under appliances, behind the toilet, and under the sink — exactly where you'd want to place a sensor.

Matter/Apple Home support

The Flood S Gen4 is Matter-certified and supports both Wi-Fi and Zigbee, so it works with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, SmartThings, and Home Assistant. Once added to Apple Home, the automation possibilities expand significantly:

  • The moment a leak is detected, cut power to the washing machine or dishwasher (if connected to a smart plug)
  • Trigger every smart bulb in the home
  • Receive a simple leak notification on your iPhone (especially handy when you're not home)

Modes, alerts, and battery life

In addition to phone notifications, it has a built-in local alarm, so you'll hear it even if you're home and your phone is in another room. Shelly offers two operating modes (flood detection and rainfall detection) along with three alert settings (intense, normal, and economy), letting you balance leak detection speed against battery life. With the included CR123A battery, it can last up to two years.

Wrap-up

At under US$30, this is the kind of accessory you'd buy three or four of without hesitation. Place one in front of the water heater, in front of the dishwasher, under the washing machine, and under the kitchen sink. Matter/Apple Home support means you can receive alerts in the Home app and build Apple Home automations around it. There's a lot to appreciate about this product, and I can't find any flaws. Honestly, a leak sensor is one of the smartest investments you can make for your smart home.

You can pick up the Shelly Flood S Gen4 on Amazon or directly from Shelly.
